newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police break up anti-privatisation protest.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police break up anti-privatisation protest.

text.p: Turkish police on Wednesday broke up a sit-in protest by more than 1,000 workers in central Turkey against the privatisation of their tyre-making company, a union official said.
"This morning all 1,154 Petlas workers in Kirsehir staged a sit-in," said Ilyas Kostekli, research director at chemical industry union Petrol-Is.
"Several hundred (gendarmerie police) came to the factory and entered the building, calling for those not working to leave," he said.
The workers at the factory in the town of Kirsehir yielded to pressure from the police and left the plant to avoid any damage or violence, Kostekli said.
The sale of Petlas, for which a buyer was found earlier this month, is part of an accelerated programme of sell-offs planned by the country's Islamist-conservative coalition.
The plan faces the major challenge of a constitutional court ruling this week, which could delay the sell-off of the programme's centrepiece, Turk Telekom.

Trade unionists have criticised the Petlas sale because it guarantees that only 700 members of the current workforce will remain in their jobs and that the plant will stay in operation for three years.
